findings.title: The previously failing symbol-rendering path is fixed and pinned by a real-CLI fixture
findings.description: `product_of_symbols` now declares `str` and splits on `,`, which matches what production actually hands it: `debug_reads._REQUESTS` selects `symbols` as `TEXT[]`, and `tick_debug_cmds._cell` (src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_debug_cmds.py:95-100) renders the `isinstance(value, list)` branch as `",".join(...)`, so `mt data tick debug requests --json` rows carry `"symbols": "ES.FUT"`. `test/unit/scripts/test_cutover_304_checks.py::test_bar_job_dirs_read_the_rows_the_real_cli_renders` builds its fixture through the real `_cell`, satisfying the project's parsing rule (fixtures must use the format production consumes). `bar_job_dirs` and `retry_exhausted_requests` — the two production callers — are both reachable with that shape.

findings.title: `calendar_for`, `_unaccounted` and `over_sessions` no longer take the weaker path
findings.description: `calendar_for` delegates to `constants.calendar_for_product` and translates only the exception type (`KeyError` → `CutoverError(exc.args[0])`), so the product-to-calendar map stays single-sourced in `FUTURES_PRODUCT_CALENDAR` with no duplicated message. `purchase_verdicts._unaccounted` now raises `CutoverError` for a bucket outside the four known sets instead of falling through as "accounted for", and `_LISTED_NEVER` buckets are skipped before it is reached — the same drift guard `tick_status_render._BUCKET_ROWS`' assert provides. `purchase_accounting.over_sessions` uses `v['raw_symbol'] or v['instrument_id']`, matching the renderer's fallback at tick_status_render.py:216. The `universe.py` comment no longer miscounts the want tuple.

findings.title: `EXIT_USAGE` is defined and never referenced
findings.description: This change replaces `START_FILE`/`BASELINE_FILE` with `EXIT_USAGE = 2`, but nothing in the module reads it: `main` returns the argparse code directly (`return int(exc.code or 0)` at scripts/cutover_304_first_purchase.py:243) and the tests assert the literal `2`. Either route the usage exit through the constant (so the value has one home, per "one value, one source") or drop it.

findings.title: The scripts-test bootstrap is copied into four modules
findings.description: `SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts"` plus a module-level `_load` that inserts `SCRIPTS` into `sys.path` and imports by name now appears in `test_cutover_304_checks.py`, `test_cutover_304_first_purchase.py`, `test_purchase_accounting.py` and `test_purchase_verdicts.py` — this change adds the last two. The testing rules call for `conftest.py` to hold shared fixtures and for individual test files to stay clean; a `test/unit/scripts/conftest.py` holding `SCRIPTS` and a `load` fixture would remove four copies and one duplicated path computation. Not blocking.

findings.title: `product_of_symbols` would surface an `AttributeError` if a caller ever hands it a list
findings.description: `symbols.split(",")` assumes the comma-joined rendering. `main` maps `CutoverError`, `subprocess.CalledProcessError`, `OSError`, `KeyError` and `ValueError` to a narrated `FAILED:` line, but not `AttributeError`, so a payload that carried the raw `TEXT[]` list would produce a traceback rather than a stop in the record. Every current caller goes through `--json` and `_cell`, so this is latent rather than live; a one-line `isinstance` normalisation with the existing `CutoverError` message would close it.

structured_findings.summary: The previously failing symbol-rendering path is fixed and pinned by a real-CLI fixture
`calendar_for`, `_unaccounted` and `over_sessions` no longer take the weaker path
The scripts-test bootstrap is copied into four modules
`product_of_symbols` would surface an `AttributeError` if a caller ever hands it a list
